title: Eight Indian-Origin US Nationals Missing Near Nepal-China Border as Families Plead for Help
excerpt: Group of pilgrims from Telangana and Karnataka lost contact at Rasuwagadhi crossing on August 26, part of wider disaster leaving hundreds of foreign tourists unaccounted for.
body:
• Eight Indian-origin US citizens, mostly from Telangana and Karnataka, have been uncontactable since August 26 near the Nepal-China border at Rasuwagadhi.
  • The group was traveling to Mount Kailash-Mansarovar through a Nepal-based agency, Classic Vacations, which families say has been unresponsive.
  • Nepal Tourism Board reports at least 65 US nationals among hundreds of foreigners still missing from the catastrophic floods that struck the border region.
  • Families have appealed to Indian and Nepalese authorities, the Indian Embassy in Kathmandu, and the US State Department for immediate intervention.

Families Sound Alarm Over Missing Pilgrims

The families of eight Indian-origin US citizens have issued an urgent appeal for help after the group became unreachable following the catastrophic floods near the Nepal-China border on August 26.

https://x.com/ANI/status/2093288361780019642

The missing persons have been identified as Laxminath Gopisetty, Sudhindra Yapalparvi, Sudhir Rangu, Keshav Rao Tadipatri, Vivek Shankar Srivastav, Venkataraman Balasubramanyam, Venkatakrishna Bangalore Raghunatharao, and Kriti Kumar Acharya. All eight are US citizens with roots in Telangana and Karnataka, according to their families.

The group was traveling to Mount Kailash-Mansarovar through Nepal under arrangements facilitated by Classic Vacations, a Nepal-based travel agency. Their last known contact was around 8:30 a.m. Nepal local time on August 26, when they were at the Rasuwagadhi Immigration Office near the Nepal-China border — the same crossing point where the devastating floods struck.

"We have made repeated attempts to contact the group following the last communication from Rasuwagadhi. There has been no response from the travel agency despite attempts to contact it."

— Families of the missing group, in a public appeal

A Disaster of Staggering Scale

The eight missing Americans are part of a much larger humanitarian crisis. The Nepal Tourism Board has reported that at least 65 US nationals are among hundreds of foreign tourists unaccounted for after flash floods triggered by a glacial lake outburst devastated communities along the Nepal-China border.

The initial flood occurred near the Gyirong Port border crossing, a major transit point for trade and religious tourism, particularly pilgrimage tours to Mount Kailash — a site sacred in Hinduism, Buddhism, and Jainism. The floods wiped out entire villages and destroyed critical infrastructure in the steep mountain gorges.

According to CNN, the US State Department has confirmed that approximately 90 Americans remain missing. The Nepal Tourism Board has also reported 178 Indian nationals, 35 Australians, 33 British citizens, and 25 Canadians among the unaccounted. On the Chinese side of the border, at least 260 foreign nationals are among more than 550 still missing, according to Chinese state media.

Families Frustrated by Lack of Information

The families of the eight missing Telangana and Karnataka natives said travel arrangements were coordinated through Anil Goel, based in the US, who collaborated with Chet Prasad Bhatta, described as the managing director of Classic Vacations. The families allege the travel agency has been unresponsive since the disaster, and that its Mumbai office provided limited assistance.

Their frustration mirrors that of other American families. Ashna and Shreya Ahuja from Texas told the BBC that their parents, Deepak and Madhu Ahuja, were crossing from Tibet into Nepal as part of Deepak's 60th birthday celebration when the floods hit. They said they had contacted the US State Department and embassies in India, Nepal, and China but received no information.

A 14-year-old American girl, Rashi Shashidharan from New York, and her mother Rekha are also among the missing. Rashi's uncle Shekhar Agrawal described feeling "helpless" and urged authorities to share information with families during what he called "the crucial golden hour."

Diaspora Connection

The missing group underscores the deep connection between the Indian-American community and religious pilgrimage to Mount Kailash. Many of the missing foreign nationals were South Asian diaspora members who had saved for months or years to make the sacred journey. The pilgrimage route through Nepal into Tibet remains one of the most popular ways for devotees worldwide to reach the holy mountain.

The families have appealed to the Government of India, the Indian Embassy in Nepal, Nepalese authorities, and immigration officials for immediate intervention. They have asked anyone with information about the group's movements near Rasuwagadhi on August 26 to contact them.

What's Next

President Donald Trump has said the US is willing to send "any help" to Nepal, calling the disaster "terrible." Search and rescue operations continue in the affected border region, though the rugged terrain and ongoing flood risks from barrier lakes formed by the disaster are complicating efforts. Nepal, China, and multiple foreign governments have deployed aid and rescue teams to the area.
image_caption: An aerial view shows houses buried in sludge following the catastrophic flooding near the Nepal-China border. Hundreds of foreign tourists, including at least 90 Americans, remain unaccounted for after the disaster.
